note: Real NOAA ISD airport records (METAR and SYNOP), 2016-2024. RH is derived from dew point. Injected faults are injected. NOAA agreement is not ground truth. See docs/WHAT_WE_DO_NOT_CLAIM.md.

DEV.title: DEV: the six stations we were allowed to tune on, 2020-2021
DEV.subtitle: Tuning happened here. These numbers are the optimistic ones.

headline.title: Headline
headline.caption: Five separate numbers. They are never merged.

rows.question: False alarms on clean real data (nothing injected)
rows.answer: 1.9% (1.8-2.0) of 98340 samples got FAULT or SUSPECT; 0.0% (0.0-0.0) got FAULT

rows.question: What happens to real extreme weather (cyclones, heat, cold, sharp fronts; nothing injected)
rows.answer: FAULT on 0.0% (0.0-0.1) of 3503 samples (0 of 30 windows); WEATHER on 10.8%, SUSPECT on 9.0%

rows.question: Injected faults whose alarm the fault raised (each type on its own; injected, not real)
rows.answer: frozen 100%; spike 98%; level shift 97%; noise burst 78%; dropout 99%; clock 3 h out 97%

rows.question: Agreement with NOAA's own quality flags (another automated system, not ground truth)
rows.answer: escalated (FAULT, SUSPECT or WEATHER) on 66.9% of 236 NOAA-flagged values (FAULT or SUSPECT alone: 22.9%); escalated on 4.7% of the 101736 values NOAA left alone

rows.question: Slow drift (health monitor, single station, no reference)
rows.answer: false drift claims on 1.1% of 3859 station-days; an injected ramp reaching 8x the service limit was found in 56% of trials

detection.title: 1. Detection of injected faults, by type (the fault raised the alarm)
detection.caption: Alarm = FAULT or SUSPECT on a sample that was NOT an alarm on the same series without the fault (paired), from the first faulty sample to the last plus 60 minutes. The faults are injected, not real. Ablation rows switch one layer off; baseline rows are simpler systems on the same data.

rows.configuration: AtmosGuard: median minutes to the alarm

detection_named.title: 1c. How AtmosGuard names what it detects, and the WEATHER-masking check
detection_named.caption: A FAULT verdict names the problem; SUSPECT asks for review. The last row is the risk of the coherent-level WEATHER route: a fault that was not alarmed but made samples look like real weather.

rows.AtmosGuard, injected faults: missed, but made some samples look like WEATHER

detection_registered.title: 1b. The same, by the criterion registered in the protocol (any alarm in the window)
detection_registered.caption: Background false alarms (about 2 % of samples) also fall inside long fault windows, so this flatters long faults (frozen 48 h, clock shift 4 days) and every system, baselines included. Kept because it was registered before the holdout.

rows.configuration: AtmosGuard: median minutes to the alarm

clean.title: 2. False alarms on clean real data
clean.caption: No fault injected. Extreme-weather windows and NOAA-flagged values removed.

extreme_weather.title: 3. Real extreme weather (nothing injected)
extreme_weather.caption: A FAULT here is a failure: real weather called a broken sensor. WEATHER is the escalated, correct verdict.

noaa.title: 4. Agreement with NOAA's own quality flags
noaa.caption: NOAA's flags come from another automated system. Agreement means consistency with existing practice, not proof of real-world accuracy.

rows.measure: AtmosGuard alarmed (FAULT or SUSPECT) on flagged values
AtmosGuard escalated at all (also WEATHER) on flagged values
AtmosGuard escalated at all on those

drift.title: 5. Slow drift, judged by the health monitor
drift.caption: A ramp over 45 days is added to one channel of clean real data. Severity = offset at the end of the ramp in multiples of the service limit (T 0.5 C, P 1 hPa, RH 3 %). One station, no reference: small drifts cannot be told from weather.

tradeoff.title: No single simpler system is good at every fault type
tradeoff.caption: Each system's weakest fault type from table 1, beside its false-alarm rate and its record on real extreme weather. A system that is best at one fault type is blind to another; the layers exist for coverage, and the WEATHER verdict exists so that coverage does not cost real storms.
